sentence: The adrenal glands are a pair of small, triangular endocrine glands, one lying on the upper surface of each kidney.
note: StatPearls: paired triangular organs on the superior aspect of each kidney. Society for Endocrinology: two small glands on top of the kidneys.

sentence: Each has an outer cortex that makes steroid hormones such as cortisol and aldosterone, and an inner medulla that makes adrenaline and noradrenaline for the fight-or-flight response.
note: OpenStax: cortex makes steroids, medulla makes epinephrine and norepinephrine. Society for Endocrinology: adrenaline and noradrenaline prepare the body for fight or flight.

sentence: Together they help the body respond to stress and regulate salt and water balance.
note: Society for Endocrinology: cortisol has a very important role in helping the body respond to stress; aldosterone regulates salt and water.

sentence: On the upper surface of each kidney, within the renal (Gerota's) fascia
note: StatPearls: located on the superior aspect of each kidney; glands sit on top of each kidney within the renal (Gerota's) fascia.

sentence: Triangular overall; the right gland is pyramid-like and the left more crescent-shaped
note: StatPearls: triangular-shaped organs; right gland has a pyramid-like form, left gland a more crescentic configuration.

sentence: Outer cortex in three zones and inner medulla, within a connective tissue capsule
note: OpenStax: cortex and medulla surrounded by a connective tissue capsule. StatPearls physiology: the cortex has three zones.

sentence: Aldosterone (outer zone), cortisol (middle zone) and androgens (inner zone)
note: OpenStax: glomerulosa mineralocorticoids, fasciculata glucocorticoids, reticularis androgens. StatPearls: aldosterone, cortisol and androgens by zone.

sentence: Adrenaline and noradrenaline
note: OpenStax: the medulla produces the amine hormones epinephrine and norepinephrine.

sentence: Superior suprarenal (from the inferior phrenic), middle suprarenal and renal artery branches
note: StatPearls: inferior phrenic arteries branch to the superior suprarenal artery; middle suprarenal arteries; renal artery contributes on the same side.

sentence: One vein per gland; the left drains into the left renal vein
note: StatPearls: a single adrenal vein drains each gland; the left adrenal vein drains into the left renal vein.

sentence: Each adrenal gland is a small, triangular organ that sits on the upper surface of a kidney, within the renal (Gerota's) fascia.
note: StatPearls: triangular-shaped organs on the superior aspect of each kidney; glands sit on top of each kidney within the renal (Gerota's) fascia.

sentence: The glands are also known as the suprarenal glands.
note: StatPearls chapter title: Adrenal Glands (Suprarenal Glands).

sentence: The two glands differ in shape: the right gland is pyramid-like, whereas the left has a more crescent-like form.
note: StatPearls: the right adrenal gland has a pyramid-like morphology, the left a more crescentic configuration.

sentence: The right gland lies close to the liver, behind the inferior vena cava and in front of the diaphragm.
note: StatPearls: the right gland sits below the liver, posterior to the inferior vena cava and anterior to the diaphragm.

sentence: The two layers of each gland have different embryonic origins: the cortex is derived from mesoderm, whereas the medulla is derived from neural crest cells.
note: StatPearls: the adrenal cortex is derived from mesoderm; the adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells.

sentence: Each gland has an outer cortex of glandular tissue and an inner medulla of nervous tissue, all surrounded by a connective tissue capsule.
note: OpenStax: outer cortex of glandular tissue, inner medulla of nervous tissue, all surrounded by a connective tissue capsule.

sentence: The cortex is organised into three zones, and each zone makes a different class of steroid hormone from cholesterol.
note: StatPearls physiology: three functional and histological zones; each layer produces steroid hormones from cholesterol. OpenStax: three hormone classes.

sentence: The outermost zona glomerulosa makes mineralocorticoids, mainly aldosterone, which affect fluid and electrolyte balance.
note: OpenStax: mineralocorticoids come from the zona glomerulosa and affect fluid and electrolyte balance; aldosterone is the main one.

sentence: The middle zona fasciculata makes glucocorticoids, chiefly cortisol, which affect glucose metabolism.
note: OpenStax: glucocorticoids from the zona fasciculata affect glucose metabolism; cortisol raises blood glucose. StatPearls: cortisol in humans.

sentence: The innermost zona reticularis releases only small amounts of androgens, which may supplement the sex hormones released from the gonads.
note: OpenStax: androgens come from the zona reticularis; the cortex releases only small amounts, which may supplement gonadal sex hormones.

sentence: The medulla at the core of the gland makes the amine hormones adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), and adrenaline is the main one.
note: OpenStax: medulla produces the amine hormones epinephrine and norepinephrine; epinephrine is the primary medulla hormone.

sentence: The adrenal glands are highly vascular.
note: StatPearls: the adrenal glands are highly vascularised.

sentence: Arterial blood reaches each gland from several sources: the superior suprarenal arteries (branches of the inferior phrenic arteries), the middle suprarenal arteries, and a contribution from the renal artery on the same side.
note: StatPearls: inferior phrenic arteries branch to become the superior suprarenal artery; middle suprarenal arteries; renal artery also contributes on the same side.

sentence: Each gland is drained by a single adrenal vein that emerges at its hilum.
note: StatPearls: a single consolidated adrenal vein emerges at the hilum and drains the entire gland.

sentence: On the left, the adrenal vein drains into the left renal vein, because the left gland lies farther from the inferior vena cava.
note: StatPearls: the left adrenal vein drains into the left renal vein, since the left gland is farther from the inferior vena cava.

sentence: The medulla receives preganglionic sympathetic nerve fibres, which release acetylcholine to stimulate the release of adrenaline and noradrenaline.
note: OpenStax: medulla hormone release is stimulated by acetylcholine from preganglionic sympathetic fibres innervating the adrenal medulla.

sentence: The medulla drives the short-term fight-or-flight response: adrenaline, together with noradrenaline, prepares the body for action and is released in response to sympathetic nervous system signals.
note: OpenStax: medulla drives the short-term fight-or-flight response via sympathetic signals. Society for Endocrinology: adrenaline with noradrenaline prepares the body for fight or flight.

sentence: The cortex drives the long-term response, through a pathway that runs from the hypothalamus, through ACTH released from the anterior pituitary, to the release of cortisol from the cortex.
note: OpenStax chapter review: long-term pathway runs from the hypothalamus through ACTH to corticosteroid release. StatPearls: ACTH is released from the anterior pituitary.

sentence: Cortisol regulates a wide range of processes, including metabolism and the immune response, and has an important role in helping the body respond to stress.
note: Society for Endocrinology: cortisol regulates processes including metabolism and the immune response and has a very important role in the stress response.

sentence: As cortisol levels rise, they slow the release of corticotrophin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus and of ACTH from the pituitary, which forms a feedback loop.
note: Society for Endocrinology: rising cortisol slows release of CRH from the hypothalamus and ACTH from the pituitary (long and short loop inhibition).

sentence: Aldosterone's main role is to regulate salt and water in the body, which affects blood pressure.
note: Society for Endocrinology: aldosterone's main role is to regulate salt and water, thus affecting blood pressure.

sentence: The renin-angiotensin system also drives aldosterone release, because angiotensin II stimulates the zona glomerulosa to make aldosterone.
note: StatPearls physiology: renin forms angiotensin I, ACE converts it to angiotensin II in the lung, and angiotensin II stimulates the glomerulosa to make aldosterone.

sentence: Adrenal problems can arise when the glands are overactive or underactive.
note: Society for Endocrinology: Cushing's syndrome from overactive adrenals; Addison's disease from underactive adrenals.

sentence: In Addison's disease, also called primary adrenal insufficiency, the glands are underactive and lack the hormones usually made by the cortex: cortisol, aldosterone and androgens.
note: Society for Endocrinology: Addison's disease or primary adrenal insufficiency is underactive adrenals lacking cortisol, aldosterone and androgens.

sentence: Damage to the cortex lowers hormone output, and in developed countries autoimmune disease is the usual cause.
note: NHS: damage to the outer adrenal layer (cortex) lowers hormone output. NIDDK: in developed countries autoimmune disease is the usual cause of Addison's.

sentence: Early symptoms can resemble depression or flu and include fatigue, muscle weakness, loss of appetite and weight loss, and darkening of the skin is a distinguishing feature.
note: NHS: early symptoms resemble depression or flu. NIDDK: fatigue, weakness, appetite and weight loss; skin darkening is a distinguishing feature.

sentence: An adrenal crisis, in which symptoms get worse very quickly, can be triggered by an infection, an injury or surgery and needs emergency care.
note: NHS: in adrenal crisis symptoms worsen very quickly; triggers include infection, accident or injury, surgery. NIDDK: adrenal crisis needs emergency care.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: Cushing's syndrome is caused by too much cortisol in the body.
note: NHS: Cushing's syndrome is a rare condition caused by having too much of the hormone cortisol in the body.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: Long-term high-dose steroid medicine is the most common trigger, and a non-cancerous growth on the pituitary or adrenal gland can also cause it; when the pituitary is responsible it is called Cushing's disease.
note: NHS: long-term steroid medicine is the most common trigger; non-cancerous pituitary or adrenal growths can cause it; pituitary cause is called Cushing's disease.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: Features include weight gain, a rounded red face, easy bruising, stretch marks and muscle weakness.
note: NHS: symptoms include weight gain, a rounded red face, easy bruising, stretch marks and muscle weakness.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: In primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome), an adrenal gland releases too much aldosterone, most often because of a non-cancerous adrenal tumour, and blood pressure can become very high.
note: MedlinePlus: the adrenal gland releases too much aldosterone; most cases involve a noncancerous adrenal tumour; untreated it can drive very high blood pressure.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: Cancer can also arise in the gland: for adrenocortical carcinoma, surgery to remove the adrenal gland (adrenalectomy) is often used.
note: NCI: adrenalectomy is often used to treat adrenocortical carcinoma, sometimes with removal of nearby lymph nodes.

where: section:Clinical relevance: excess hormones and tumours
sentence: Phaeochromocytoma is a tumour of the adrenal gland that releases excess adrenaline and noradrenaline and can cause intense episodes lasting a short time, known as paroxysmal attacks.
note: NCI pheochromocytoma pages: adrenal tumour with excess adrenaline and noradrenaline; paroxysmal attacks are intense episodes lasting a short time.

where: section:How the adrenal glands are investigated
sentence: Because symptoms such as fatigue and weakness are non-specific, they need assessment by a clinician.
note: NIDDK: symptoms are often nonspecific, which can delay diagnosis. NHS: early symptoms resemble more common conditions. Referral to a clinician is a standard safety statement.

where: section:How the adrenal glands are investigated
sentence: In suspected Addison's disease, blood tests measure sodium, potassium and cortisol.
note: NHS: blood tests measure the levels of sodium, potassium and cortisol; abnormal results may indicate Addison's disease.

where: section:How the adrenal glands are investigated
sentence: The ACTH stimulation test is the test used most often to diagnose adrenal insufficiency, and blood tests can also detect antibodies in autoimmune Addison's disease.
note: NIDDK: the ACTH stimulation test is used most often to diagnose adrenal insufficiency; blood tests can detect antibodies in autoimmune Addison's.

where: section:How the adrenal glands are investigated
sentence: For suspected Cushing's syndrome, cortisol can be checked in blood, urine or saliva, and a high result leads to referral to an endocrinologist, who may arrange further blood tests and scans.
note: NHS: GP can check cortisol in blood, urine or saliva; high results lead to endocrinologist referral and further tests. NIDDK: cortisol testing.

where: section:How the adrenal glands are investigated
sentence: Diagnosis is based on the medical history, a physical examination and laboratory tests.
note: NIDDK: diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome is based on medical history, physical exam and lab tests.
